blogs.title: Forget to Breathe: Central Hypoventilation Mimicking Ondine’s Curse in Chiari Malformation
blogs.description: Explores the pathophysiology of brainstem compression in Chiari I, specifically the dissociation between voluntary and automatic breathing. Discusses why patients may present with severe 'silent hypoxia' (70-80% sats) without the sensation of air hunger due to disrupted interoceptive pathways.

blogs.title: The Normal Scope Trap: Recognizing Neurogenic Dysphagia in Posterior Fossa Pathology
blogs.description: Analyzes the diagnostic challenge of dysphagia affecting both solids and liquids with normal endoscopic findings. Highlights the need to consider brainstem compression and lower cranial nerve dysfunction when mechanical obstruction is ruled out by ENT and GI workups.

blogs.title: 14 Years in the Archives: The Critical Value of Re-Reading Historical Imaging
blogs.description: Focuses on the missed CT finding from a trauma 14 years prior that was overlooked until re-review. Discusses the importance of retrieving and critically re-evaluating historical imaging in patients with chronic, undiagnosed neurological symptoms.

blogs.title: Haircut for Headache: Vertex Allodynia as a Neurologic Red Flag
blogs.description: Examines the unique headache phenotype described in this case, including vertex pain and cutaneous allodynia relieved by cutting hair. Discusses the association between occipital neuralgia, burning vertex syndrome, and posterior fossa crowding in Chiari malformation.

blogs.title: The Chiari Conundrum: Incidental Anatomical Variant or Pathological Malformation?
blogs.description: Addresses the clinical tension regarding Chiari I findings in asymptomatic individuals. Reviews contemporary evidence on the spectrum of posterior fossa volumetric mismatch and guides clinicians on distinguishing incidental findings from symptomatic Chiari syndrome requiring intervention.

blogs.title: Anxiety vs. Anatomy: Avoiding the Psychiatric Label in Unexplained Hypoxia
blogs.description: Discusses the diagnostic delay caused by attributing hypoxic episodes and choking to anxiety or panic attacks. Provides a framework for clinicians to recognize organic brainstem causes when patients present with unexplained desaturation and lack of respiratory distress.
